item.title: ATLAS finds hints of the hidden structure of the vacuum
item.description: Researchers at the University of Bonn, together with colleagues from Oxford and Prague, played a leading role in analyzing particle collisions at CERN's Large Hadron Collider. The ATLAS Collaboration observed more proton collisions with the particle pattern it was looking for than expected. This could point to a phenomenon predicted by the Standard Model of particle physics that has never been directly observed, known as QCD instanton processes. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Fine particle pollution may weaken spring greening by clogging leaf pores
item.description: Each spring, warmer temperatures can bring earlier leaf-out, while rising atmospheric carbon dioxide can stimulate plant growth, allowing land ecosystems to absorb more carbon. Yet a study published in Nature Plants on Nov. 27 finds that this climate-driven greening has an overlooked brake: fine particulate air pollution, or PM2.5. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ozone hole one of the largest in decades
item.description: In contrast to the 2025 seasonal ozone hole above Antarctica, which was the fifth smallest since 1992, this year's ozone hole ranks as one of the largest in 48 years, based on long-term atmospheric observations, including data from the Copernicus Sentinel-5P satellite. While this may sound alarming, it is important to remember that the size of the ozone hole varies naturally from year to year, and the long-term recovery of the ozone layer remains on track. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Robots, not astronauts, will have to fix space data centers
item.description: Yesterday we explored some of the difficulties facing orbital data centers in our look at the bottleneck of launching enough solar panels and radiative cooling systems to power the AI computing boom in space. JPL physicist Dr. Slava Turyshev, who wrote the paper at the center of that article, also published a follow-up study in August, available on the arXiv preprint server, about how getting the hardware off the ground is only half the battle. Once all that equipment is up there, someone, or something, is going to have to maintain it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: As families gather for Thanksgiving, college science students need training to talk across societal divides
item.description: Most Americans have seen it happen. Relatives argue online about whether vaccines are safe and effective. Friends and neighbors trade jabs over climate change and whether anything should be done about it. Public officials and scientists disagree, loudly, about what causes autism or which vaccines children should get and when. No one gives an inch, and the rifts rarely heal. This Thanksgiving, after a contentious election season, many of those conversations will happen face to face around the dinner table. Fuente: Phys.org.

Dos meses después, como suele hacer, la Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (AEMET) repasó el invierno y llegó a la conclusión de que, con la información disponible, nada de lo que pasó en aquellos cinco días podía considerarse una ola de frío. item.title: New fern species discovered after nearly 200 years of being mistaken for another
item.description: Chinese researchers have formally described a new fern species that has been hiding in plain sight for nearly 200 years. Named Drynaria lineatisora, the species was collected as early as the 19th century in Myanmar and Vietnam, but it was repeatedly misidentified as the widespread Drynaria coronans. Recent field studies by researchers from the Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanical Garden (XTBG) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and their collaborators confirmed that it is indeed a distinct species. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The dark matter puzzle deepens: Nearby galaxies challenge cosmic simulations
item.description: Galaxies appear to hold a surprise beneath their visible stars: Their inner regions contain less dark matter than some of our most advanced simulations predict. By measuring these movements, astronomers can reconstruct where this unseen matter lies and test the computer simulations used to understand the universe. A study of 136 nearby galaxies, involving the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (IAC), reveals a discrepancy that becomes more extensive in more massive systems, offering fresh clues… Fuente: Phys.org.
